pack.name: GRC Assessment Survey Question Banks
pack.description: Pre-built survey question banks for GRC assessments: vendor/third-party risk assessment, control self-assessment (CSA), and IT general controls questionnaire. Ready to launch or customize per tenant.
pack.author: GovernexPlus

items.name: Third-Party Risk Assessment Questionnaire
items.description: Standard vendor/third-party risk assessment covering information security controls, data handling practices, business continuity, compliance, and subcontractor management. Suitable for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendor assessments.

questions.text: Does your organization have a documented Information Security Policy approved by senior management?
Does your organization have a dedicated CISO or equivalent role responsible for information security?
Is your organization certified against ISO/IEC 27001 or SOC 2?
When was your most recent third-party security assessment or penetration test?
Is multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforced for all users accessing systems that process our data?
Is user access reviewed and recertified at least annually?
Is access promptly revoked upon employee termination (within 24 hours)?
Is privileged access (admin accounts) controlled via PAM or equivalent?
Is data encrypted at rest using AES-256 or equivalent?
Is data encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher?
Do you maintain a data processing register identifying where our data is stored and processed?
What is your data retention policy for data processed on our behalf?
Do you have a documented Incident Response Plan that has been tested within the last 12 months?
What is your contractual commitment for notifying us of security incidents affecting our data?
Describe your incident response capability (team, tools, and process).
Do you have a tested Business Continuity Plan (BCP) and Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP)?
What is your Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for services provided to us?
When was your last DR test performed?
Do you use subcontractors or sub-processors that will handle our data?
If yes, do you perform risk assessments on these subcontractors?
Please list the primary subcontractors/sub-processors involved in our services.

items.name: Control Self-Assessment (CSA) Survey
items.description: Annual control self-assessment questionnaire for business unit managers. Covers key COSO control objectives: control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information/communication, and monitoring.

questions.text: Management in my area demonstrates commitment to ethical behavior and integrity.
Responsibilities for key controls are clearly defined and communicated.
Staff receive adequate training on relevant controls and compliance requirements.
Key risks in my area are identified and documented.
Risk assessments are updated when significant changes occur in my area.
I am aware of the top risks in my business area and the controls in place.
Appropriate controls exist to mitigate key risks in my area.
Controls are performed consistently and as documented.
Segregation of duties is maintained for critical processes in my area.
Identify any controls in your area that you believe are not operating effectively.
I receive timely and accurate information needed to perform my control responsibilities.
Control deficiencies and issues are communicated to management promptly.
Management monitoring activities (reviews, reconciliations) are performed regularly.
Control deficiencies identified are remediated in a timely manner.
Describe any significant control weaknesses or gaps you are aware of in your area.

items.name: IT General Controls Questionnaire
items.description: IT manager self-assessment questionnaire covering the four ITGC domains: logical access controls, change management, computer operations, and data backup/recovery. Used for annual ITGC attestation.

questions.text: User access is provisioned only upon documented management authorization.
Terminated user access is revoked within 24 hours.
Privileged access is reviewed quarterly.
User access is reviewed annually (or more frequently for privileged roles).
All production changes are authorized via the change management process before implementation.
Developers do not have the ability to migrate their own changes to production.
Emergency changes follow the documented emergency change procedure.
Critical batch jobs are monitored for successful completion.
Job failures are alerted to operations staff and resolved per documented procedures.
System availability is monitored with alerts for threshold breaches.
Production system data is backed up daily.
Backup recovery has been successfully tested within the last 12 months.
Backups are stored in a geographically separate location.
